## What this dashboard shows

- Working capital positions across five Wipro Enterprises companies at 2026-07, showing cash, receivables, payables, and collection/payment timing metrics (DSO and DPO).
- Wipro Consumer Care International holds the largest working capital balances with ₹311.37B cash, ₹245.89B receivables, and ₹365.44B payables.
- Data is sourced from multiple ERP systems including real and simulated SAP, SAP S/4HANA (two systems), Oracle EBS, Microsoft Dynamics 365, and Tally Prime.

## What to report

- Wipro Consumer Care International shows exceptional payment terms with 612 DPO versus 207 DSO, resulting in a favorable -406 day spread (collecting before paying).
- Wipro Infrastructure Engineering maintains ₹87.28B cash with 103 DSO and 234 DPO (-131 day spread).
- Wipro GE Healthcare demonstrates balanced working capital with matched DSO and DPO at 73 days each (DSO − DPO of 0).
- Wipro Consumer Care India and Wipro Kawasaki Precision Machinery show modest working capital positions with ₹110.04B and ₹35.58B cash respectively, and negative DSO-DPO spreads of -29 and -24 days.

## Watch out for

- SAP companies display open items as recorded in source ERP (real SAP data for Wipro Consumer Care International includes unapplied customer credits and uncleared supplier items), causing DSO/DPO to sit outside typical ranges—the 612 DPO figure requires verification.
- The 207 DSO at Wipro Consumer Care International appears unusually high and warrants investigation into collection efficiency or outstanding credit issues.
- Mixed data sources include both real and simulated SAP data; clarify which companies rely on simulated versus actual data for accuracy assessment.
- Question to ask: Are the extreme DSO/DPO figures at Wipro Consumer Care International driven by timing of open item clearing, or do they reflect genuine working capital management concerns?
